lead.title: NVIDIA clarifies its local-AI lineup: DGX Spark 64GB, RTX Spark and DGX Station
lead.summary: At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA split its local-AI hardware into three lines: the DGX Spark 64GB (GB10 Grace Blackwell, from $4,999, shipping via Acer, ASUS, Dell, Gigabyte, HP and MSI), the Windows-based RTX Spark with up to 128GB unified memory and 1 PFLOP of AI compute, and DGX Station for enterprise. DGX Spark now supports manual clusters of up to eight units — 1TB of pooled memory on 128GB models — via NVIDIA Sync Cluster Assistant, with llama.cpp and vLLM acceleration updates for Qwen 3.8 and other open models.

top_stories.title: Heretic 2.0 ships: Arbitrary-Rank Ablation replaces classic abliteration
top_stories.summary: The biggest release yet for the model-modification tool makes Arbitrary-Rank Ablation the default steering method, rebuilds the project around a plugin system, and adds non-interactive runs with end-to-end tests; 1.x config files break and need the migration guide.

top_stories.title: Karpathy ships HackerTube in about two hours with Claude Opus 5.5
top_stories.summary: A Hacker News-curated YouTube alternative that filters 43M HN comments over 20 years down to 6,454 repeatedly recommended videos, with no login required.

top_stories.title: SemiAnalysis releases GDPx, a frontier-level agentic benchmark — best model scores 12%
top_stories.summary: A new agentic benchmark across high-value economic domains built with specialized data partners; even the best model scores just 12%, and the team argues the first trillion dollars of AI revenue will concentrate in sectors deploying frontier intelligence at high ROI.

top_stories.title: DoorDash to acquire Instacart for $17B
top_stories.summary: M&A: DoorDash agrees to acquire Instacart for $17 billion; DoorDash noted in Q3 earnings it has so far received only a few hundred orders from AI agents.

items.title: Latent-Lens: visual perception in small language models through latent communication
items.summary: Replaces lossy discrete-text bottlenecks between VLMs and small language models with latent-space communication, improving spatial and fine-grained perception in modular SLM systems.

items.title: There Is No Free Loop: when does looping a trained model pay for its inference compute?
items.summary: Characterizes when looping a block of layers in a trained model — constant parameter count, memory footprint and training cost — pays off against the extra per-token inference compute.

items.title: In-model context compression with agentic soft tokens for long-horizon LLM agents
items.summary: Compresses growing agent contexts inside the model itself via agentic soft tokens, cutting the computational cost of long-horizon interactions without external compressor modules.

items.title: MUON-RT reuses the teacher's trajectory for momentum-free Muon self-distillation
items.summary: Reuses the EMA teacher's stored update history in self-distillation instead of a separate momentum buffer, reducing persistent training memory for LLM fine-tuning.

items.title: SparseGDN: chunk sparse computation in linear attention
items.summary: Hardware-aware sparse chunk computation for Gated Delta Networks reduces the cost of long-context prefill — dense intra-chunk work, recurrent-state updates and state storage — in linear-attention models.

items.title: DeepSeek V4.1-Flash: smallest model in the new architecture family
items.summary: DeepSeek launches V4.1-Flash, the smallest model in its new architecture family, with greater capability, faster inference and higher throughput; weights on Hugging Face as deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017.

items.title: KRAFTON releases Raon-1-mini-preview: 30B-A4B MoE trained from scratch
items.summary: Apache-2.0 30B-A4B Mixture-of-Experts language model with a hybrid Raon Delta Attention + Gated MLA layout, 262K context, untied LM head, and a GGUF variant for local runtimes.

items.title: tmax-9b-v1.1: a terminal-agent 9B trained with DPPO on Qwen3.5-9B
items.summary: Community terminal-agent model trained on the TMax-13K v1.1 task set, Apache 2.0, evaluated on 96 TB-Lite tasks.

items.title: Arken: cryptographic identity for AI agents calling MCP servers
items.summary: Open-source scheme giving AI agents cryptographic identities when they call MCP servers and APIs, making agent-to-service calls attributable and verifiable.

items.title: Fluent 2: AI teammates that run fully on-device on macOS
items.summary: Launched on Product Hunt with AI teammate agents that run entirely on-device, keeping inference local rather than routing through a cloud API.

items.title: Rufous: an agent tuned specifically for small local models
items.summary: A coding/assistant agent attuned to the constraints of locally hosted SLMs rather than frontier cloud APIs.

items.title: Qwen3.8-27B UD-IQ4_XS Heretic + MTP quant fits a 16 GB card at 55-68 tok/s
items.summary: Community quant series reproduces Unsloth's per-tensor UD recipe on the uncensored Qwen3.8-27B Heretic build with the MTP head preserved, in 12/16/24 GB variants; MTP head precision barely affects acceptance rate, and shared GPU memory on Windows is the main decode-speed cliff.

items.title: n8n current stable 2.45.7; 2.46 line adds personal credentials in team projects
items.summary: Stable 2.45.7 brings queue-mode and IMAP trigger fixes; 2.46.0 lets personal credentials work in any team project without sharing them, and the Schedule Trigger has run on the durable scheduler by default since 2.45.

items.title: Ceva unveils four-tier NeuPro NPU portfolio for edge and on-device AI
items.summary: Nano, Prime, Max and Ultra tiers claim up to 2x higher AI throughput per mm-squared and 50% better energy efficiency on multimodal and agentic workloads, with dynamic tensor shapes and paged KV caching; general availability planned for Q2 2027.

items.title: Best GPUs for local AI (November 2026): RTX PRO 6000 tops the ranking, RX 7900 XTX best value
items.summary: The updated ranking puts the 96GB RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell first (DeepSeek V4 Flash fully in memory at ~69 tok/s at 32k context) and calls the $1,300 24GB RX 7900 XTX the best tokens-per-dollar card at ~23 tok/s on Qwen 3.8 27B.

items.title: VRAM capacity can matter more than GPU generation on an older local-AI PC
items.summary: A practical upgrade walkthrough: a Ryzen 9 5950X desktop going from 64GB to 128GB system RAM and from an RTX 3080 10GB to an RTX 3090 24GB reaches roughly 50 tokens/s on a dense Qwen 27B model — capacity decides which models fit on the GPU, bandwidth decides speed.
